harnesses.bound: Unwind 65 with unwinding assertions; digest pointer and length preservation, not exhaustive JSON or a cryptographic collision theorem.
harnesses.production: crates/domyjob-core/src/wire.rs Snapshot::without_cache called directly by Request::canonical_submission and Store::reserve; native Request contracts preserve command and full snapshot identity.

harnesses.name: storage_lifecycle::proofs::storage_is_retired_only_after_execution_and_delivery

harnesses.production: crates/domyjob-core/src/storage_lifecycle.rs retention called by Store::retire in crates/domyjob/src/store/lifecycle.rs; Store::acknowledge calls retire

harnesses.name: process_inventory::proofs::live_group_members_prevent_workspace_removal
harnesses.contract: Every admitted non-Z state, including native H and ?, blocks workspace removal in the selected group; only Z is classified as a zombie and unknown state bytes are rejected.

harnesses.bound: No loops or input assumptions; scalar row decision only, not all process-inventory strings.
harnesses.production: crates/domyjob-core/src/process_inventory.rs classify_state and Process::blocks called by group_quiescent; native parser and actual OS output are checked separately

boundaries.reason: The fast and release gate adapters depend on Actions job ordering, domyjob source snapshots, Docker image resolution, native paths, bind mounts, ownership restoration, and process exit status. These operating-system and engine contracts are outside Kani's executable model. Heavy commands run natively in Actions or in the required bounded local container.
boundaries.evidence: CI adapter tests require verifier-free inventory checks in the fast gate and exclude fuzz campaigns from ci-success. They preserve heavy selectors, opaque remote arguments, read-only source, writable output mounts, fixed resource bounds, and refusal of escaping directory links. Workflow validation checks the candidate and release job dependencies; hosted campaign results remain required before release publication.
boundaries.reconsider: Container arguments, image resolution, mount ownership, command selection or result admission changes or fails, or a verifier supports the actual Docker and filesystem boundary.

boundaries.reason: Owned child exit, concurrent output files and native scheduling are operating-system boundaries outside Kani's executable model. The adapter uses no response deadline; time controls only diagnostic reporting and polling cadence.
boundaries.evidence: The e2e_peer target drives a real gated child, captures partial output before its response, retains process/request/output-tail diagnostics on missing replies, and explicitly stops a known held child. The native bootstrap and job scenarios exercise the shared adapter. The ownership gate rejects timed reply APIs and scenario clocks in current and future e2e leaves.
boundaries.reconsider: Process ownership, output capture, response framing or watchdog reporting changes or fails, or a verifier supports these native effects.

boundaries.reason: Pure decision proofs do not establish kernel directory-handle identity, replacement races, permissions, or native filesystem durability. A job lock captures an existing private no-follow directory and creates its relative lock without recreating parents; Store rechecks the receipt when the state lock is absent.
boundaries.evidence: mise run test on each supported native host includes late_completion_does_not_recreate_a_retired_job, completion_markers_are_private_and_idempotent, a_retained_directory_cannot_mark_its_replacement, a_captured_job_lock_cannot_recreate_its_retired_directory, late_retirement_does_not_recreate_a_consumed_job_or_lose_its_receipt, a_missing_job_directory_is_never_created_by_a_lock_reader, and a_linked_job_directory_cannot_grant_a_lock_in_its_target; Unix additionally checks a_relative_job_lock_cannot_follow_a_file_link.
boundaries.reconsider: Filesystem semantics or cap-std changes, marker ownership changes, or any native directory-replacement contract fails.

boundaries.reason: The source-bound decision and counted-port proofs do not establish PowerShell compilation, filesystem publication, windows-spawn creation-time Job attachment, or Win32 accounting/termination. A retained fresh Job is attached during process creation before PowerShell can launch compiler children.
boundaries.evidence: The input_controller target covers arbitrary delays beyond the former case and operation deadlines, foreign/malformed/disappeared readiness, peer exit and primary-plus-cleanup faults. Windows preserves all eight binary input schedules; the held descendant triggers explicit cancellation after observed containment, followed by retained root reap and zero active processes. Waiting diagnostics include the root PID, request and stderr tail; the outer nextest watchdog diagnoses hangs.
boundaries.reconsider: A phase/channel, Job attachment, accounting, ownership or cleanup contract changes or fails, or a verifier supports the actual Win32/CLR boundary.

boundaries.reason: The actual admission transition depends on filesystem identity, private candidate ACLs, operating-system selection/usage locks, directory publication, and the publisher-to-node lifetime. The segmented writer proof cannot establish these effects. Selection bridges publication to final usage admission because Windows refuses renaming a directory with open child-file handles.
boundaries.evidence: Native build tests retain active and pinned installations, serialize publication and pruning, retain usage through the first node callback, and retire every superseded idle installation after its owned job and cache users quiesce.
boundaries.reconsider: A native publication, selection, usage, identity, or cleanup contract fails, filesystem or locking semantics change, or the first-node ownership protocol changes.

boundaries.reason: Kani verifies the actual bounded Rust segmented writer, not CLR pinning/marshalling, PowerShell stdin inheritance, or overlapped Win32 completion semantics. The prefix reader retains its borrowed pipe handle, pinned bytes, event, and operation until native completion.
boundaries.evidence: The source-bound native Windows bootstrap scenario runs the actual script in Windows PowerShell and PowerShell 7, eight SDK inherited-overlapped-input schedules with exact binary prefix/remainder/EOF, and refusal without publication for truncated input, a write-only handle, and a failed pending observer. All hosts exercise the exact original frame, snapshot digest and bytes, isolated installer input/output, one upload/first-request connection, and primary-preserving cwd/cleanup faults.
boundaries.reconsider: The actual reader, shell launcher, byte-mode pipe assumption, FFI lifetime, source prefix format, or any native handoff contract changes.

boundaries.reason: The source-bound scalar budget/read-length, finite ASCII metadata, and bounded actual std::path proofs do not establish native Git configuration and path output, canonical directory identity and case folding, declaration stability, ignore matching, concurrent mutation, capability-relative file opening, Windows reparse semantics, or tar publication. The actual source adapter captures canonical Git/common directories through individually bounded queries before top-level discovery, refuses selected metadata/bare roots or unresolved declarations, and excludes both trees after canonicalization from the merged tracked and walker paths. Git's bounded untracked-path query owns Git-ignore precedence; the walker retains .ignore and no-follow entry policy. One retained selected-root capability owns archive admission.
boundaries.evidence: Native source, source_archive, source_fingerprint and source_file tests cover Git-written global excludes paths with spaces and inherited config-count context, ignored tracked modified bytes, ignored untracked exclusion, deletion, real .GIT metadata, and subdirectory paths. Actual Git oracle fixtures cover ancestor-ignored exclusion, competing relative excludes files, repository-root anchored patterns, and separate-directory info/exclude precedence with .gitignore negation. Separate, distinct common, forced-tracked metadata and nested-selection controls require only current working bytes; malformed ancestor declarations, selected metadata/bare roots, and unresolved case aliases refuse, while valid symlink/case aliases are bound to actual canonical directories and non-Git HEAD/objects working names remain ordinary input. Finite Miri controls bind Path::components to the actual typed matcher for whole components and rooted/relative namespaces. Shared runtime/build readers retain every captured parent; Unix uses public cap-primitives open_dir_nofollow and safe rustix NOFOLLOW|NONBLOCK|CLOEXEC, while Windows NtCreateFile uses RootDirectory and OPEN_REPARSE_POINT for every component, rejecting non-disk/reparse handles before reads. Native controls replace inspected parents/final files, rename captured ancestors/root names, refuse a writerless FIFO within a killed/reaped child deadline, preserve read errors, and bound growth/truncation reads to admitted length+1. Native parser tests admit exactly MAX_PATH_BYTES in complete valid records and refuse one extra path byte separately from stream/count/record limits. Native case folding, custom bare identification without Git or an explicit declaration, and one atomic view of concurrently modified Git state/files are not claimed.
boundaries.reconsider: Git output, ancestor ignore semantics, or capability/filesystem semantics change, a native source, link, budget, collision or archive contract fails, or a verifier can check the actual Git/filesystem adapter boundary.

boundaries.reason: The source-bound ordered request-port and bounded Write-port proofs do not establish actual frame/JSON decoding, native Unix socket behavior, launchd, descriptor inheritance, concurrency, or every possible port implementation.
boundaries.evidence: Mac workspace tests exercise bounded frames without request EOF or socket deadlines, readiness and refusal with a held receiver clone, exact native causes, combined request and reply failures, and redacted packet diagnostics. The handoff and reply Miri lanes retain the production ordered ports and write/shutdown adapters.
boundaries.reconsider: Reply framing or socket semantics change, a native integration fails, or a verifier supports the actual concurrent operating-system boundary.

boundaries.reason: The finite protocol step and job-state proofs do not establish filesystem locking, worker creation, SSH reliability, or native process lifetime.
boundaries.evidence: Native workspace tests exercise duplicate and conflicting submission, the existing launch-lock boundary, finished-job retries, launch refusal, and missing-supervisor state through the production app and Store adapters.
boundaries.reconsider: The launch or store locking protocol changes, a native adapter contract fails, or a verifier supports the actual filesystem and process boundary.

boundaries.reason: Kani, Quint/Apalache, Miri, and libFuzzer execute on hosted Linux at the release gate, or in a bounded Linux container on demand. Native Windows verifier capability is not claimed.
boundaries.evidence: Release check runs mise run verify, mise run miri, and mise run fuzz on the resolved candidate SHA. Its three-OS matrix runs native workspace tests, inventory consistency, Windows SDK contracts, and fixed Windows e2e repeats. These campaigns are outside the fast push and PR gate.
boundaries.reconsider: A pinned native verifier supports Windows, the implementation adds target-specific core decisions, or any native Windows contract fails.

boundaries.reason: Kani does not establish concurrent Win32 kernel ownership or foreign-function behavior.
boundaries.evidence: mise x -- cargo xtask windows-contracts; mise run test on Windows exercises capability, child ownership, failure cleanup, and process-tree termination.
boundaries.reconsider: A verifier supports the actual Win32 boundary, SDK semantics change, or a native ownership contract fails.

boundaries.reason: Client configuration parsing, native file replacement and external client schemas are adapter boundaries outside the finite core ownership decisions.
boundaries.evidence: Cleanup fixtures retain foreign hooks and shared MCP entries, comments, malformed documents and historical chat files. Repeated cleanup is idempotent. Native file fixtures preserve linked configuration files and refuse dangling links.
boundaries.reconsider: A supported client changes its schema, ownership recognition changes or a preservation fixture fails.
